transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-01
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SE), John Park (CTO - Helios), Marta Ruiz (SRE), Evan Kim (Platform), Sophie Li (Security)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): discuss reserved capacity, isolation for PII, burst guardrails, preliminary benchmarks, compliance checklist.

00:00 Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're Alex from Redwood inference, I'm joined by Priya and Liam from our solutions team. Real quick can we do a 30 second round robin of roles?
00:12 John Park (CTO): John Park, CTO here, I'm leading product infra decisions. Marta - she will speak to ops, Evan is our platform engineer who will run the benchmarks. Sophie is on for security questions.
00:25 Marta (SRE): hi, yes thanks. we're mostly concerned about isolation and prewarm for spikes.
00:30 Priya (SE): awesome, thanks. goal today is to understand your traffic patterns, isolation needs for PII, and your expected surge profile so we can recommend reserved topology and warm pool sizing.
00:43 Alex (AE): and we'll cover host vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs but it sounds like you're leaning dedicated because of data residency?
00:50 John Park: correct, we have regulated workflows. we need guaranteed capacity and audit logs. also interested in an on-prem option eventually.
00:58 Evan (Platform): our peak 95th percentile latencies matter — for the user flows we target sub-250ms for short prompts, but during spikes that goes up. we want predictable tails.
01:10 Priya: totally. to confirm — are the PII endpoints fully isolated or just flagged? i.e., will you require tenant-fenced nodes or is encryption + audit enough?
01:22 Sophie (Security): we prefer tenant-fenced for those endpoints. encryption at rest with KMS is must; SSO/SAML and audit trails too. SOC2 is table stakes.
01:33 Alex: note: dedicated Reserved nodes can be deployed in a VPC with customer-managed routing and KMS integration. the Private on-prem path can provide air-gapped, but it adds onboarding time.
01:45 Marta: how does Redwood handle prewarm? warm pools, keep-alives, or preloading caches?
01:52 Priya: we use a warm-pool model — you reserve hot nodes (prewarmed processes) plus a cold pool. for burst we recommend a hot-pool hold based on your spike probability; we can do probabilistic sizing. caching includes prefix K V cache (sometimes shows up in transcript as K V cash) to shorten tokens for repeat flows.
02:08 Liam (SE): noted: kernel selection and quantization affect cold-start times; some models (quantized 4-bit) start faster but have different latency characteristics.
02:18 John: what's the failover story — if reserved pool is fully saturated do you offer overflow to hosted compatibility or queued requests?
02:27 Priya: we support automatic fallback policies. options are: 1) overflow to a compatible hosted variant (same model family, maybe slightly smaller), 2) degrade to a cached response, or 3) queue with SLOs. Most customers pick fallback to hosted smaller-model + rate-limit to preserve latency.
02:44 Evan: any jitter in KV cache replication across nodes? we have strict convergence needs for session continuity.
02:51 Priya: KV is per-instance for autoregressive sessions; we persist to an internal fast cache and route sticky sessions when needed. on Dedicated we can place routes on same node to reduce misses. there may be occasional mis-route during node failover.
03:06 John: ok. can we talk topology recommendations? we currently have 600 RPS steady across endpoints, with spikes to 3.5k RPS for 2-5 minutes once a day. tokens per request avg 250, heavy endpoints hit 1k tokens.
03:28 Priya: thanks, that helps. rough calc: steady would map to N reserved GPUs depending on model; for spikes you can either size hot-pool to handle 90-95% of spikes or rely on burst overlay. Given daily short spikes, we typically propose a hybrid: reserve X nodes for steady throughput + hotpool sized at Y to cover 80-90% of spikes and rely on hosted overflow for extreme tails.
03:50 Marta: we need guaranteed latency on spikes for top-3 endpoints — can you SLA that if we reserve additional warm nodes?
03:58 Alex: yes, Dedicated contracts can specify latency SLO tiers tied to reserved capacity and burst commitments. SLA requires commitment levels; we'll include targets in the pricing doc.
04:08 Sophie: compliance — how granular are audit logs? we need per-token tracing and retention for 12 months ideally.
04:16 Priya: Audit logs include request metadata, model version, route, and token counts; per-token payloads are optional (can be redacted) — retention and encryption managed via KMS. For Private we can enable longer retention in-customer storage.
04:30 Evan: about on-prem path — how intrusive is it? network and control plane understandings?
04:36 Liam: Private installs ship a small control-plane agent; compute runs in your environment or under your cloud accounts. onboarding is 6-12 weeks typically depending on procurement.
04:46 John: cost question — what's the delta between reserved capacity vs hosted overflow? we need unit economics.
04:52 Alex: pricing spreadsheet we'll share, but high-level: reserved capacity priced monthly per GPU with commit discounts; burst overlay usage billed at per-token rate plus small prewarm fee. We can model expected savings if spikes are frequent and predictable.
05:07 Marta: does Redwood support tenant-quarantine? we want the ability to isolate a noisy tenant quickly.
05:14 Priya: yes, we support tenant isolation and sharding. options: physical tenant-fencing (dedicated host) or soft fencing via scheduler quotas and eviction policies. Physical fencing is recommended for PII or noisy tenants.
05:28 Sophie: are there RBAC primitives for operator access and key rotation?
05:33 Liam: yes SSO, fine-grained RBAC, and KMS integration; customers can bring their own keys and rotate them.
05:40 John: what about deterministic prewarm time? for our heavy endpoints we need <200ms at P95 even on spike.
05:48 Priya: depends on model and input length. For 7B-ish models quantized, warm instances can hit ~120-180ms P95 for short prompts; for long tokens it rises. We'll propose benchmarks to validate.
06:02 Evan: we'll run the benchmark — can you give us the harness and synthetic profile?
06:07 Priya: yes we'll share a harness and test runner; prefer GH repo access or a temporary token.
06:12 John: security review — Sophie will request SOC2 artifacts and pen test history; typical timeline?
06:19 Alex: we can share SOC2 report and compliance pack within 48 hours, and coordinate an NDA for deeper artifacts.
06:26 Sophie: good. also curious about data residency regions — we need EU+US deployment.
06:31 Alex: we have regions in NA and EU; dedicated can be region pinned. Private provides on-prem EU.
06:36 Marta: operationally, how do updates/rollouts work for model versions? we can't have noisy regressions in production.
06:42 Priya: Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B splits, and automatic rollback on perf/quality regressions. you can pin model versions per route. We also have eval hooks for prompt sets.
06:55 John: ok great. can we simulate a failure scenario? if a reserved node fails in the middle of a spike, what's the customer-visible impact?
07:02 Priya: typical: requests routed away; if hot-pool has spare headroom we absorb; otherwise fallback triggers to hosted or smaller model. We also pre-allocate a small buffer for node loss. We'll share an incident matrix in the playbook.
07:20 Evan: for benchmarks, we want two windows: baseline steady and synthetic spike with token length distribution matching our top endpoints.
07:27 Priya: noted. we'll propose dates — early next week and a follow-up the following week.
07:33 Alex: next steps recap: I'll send pricing and the burst playbook; Priya will send the test harness and calendar invites; John will provide traffic CSV. We also agreed to a short technical deep-dive next week after the benchmark.
07:49 John: sounds good. any blockers on procurement? we may need a procurement clause for dedicated uptime SLA.
07:55 Alex: we can surface standard SLA language; procurement typically asks for uptime targets and liability caps — we'll share the template.
08:03 Sophie: for security docs send to security@helios.io and we'll route through procurement.
08:09 Alex: perfect.
08:12 Marta: one last ops note — eviction windows and preemptions: we need a playbook for failover to ensure no session loss.
08:20 Priya: we'll attach our eviction/playbook doc. it includes sticky routing and short lived session replay patterns.
08:27 John: great thanks everyone.

Auto-generated action items (end): Alex to send pricing and playbook; Priya to send harness and propose benchmarks; John to deliver traffic profile.

End of transcript.
